examples.english: Strike while the iron is hot.
examples.notes: Proverb meaning: act while conditions are favorable.

examples.japanese: {鉄|てつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{橋|はし}→橋：02163_hashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{架|か}かっている→かかる：00711_kakaru⟧。
⟦{地下鉄|ちかてつ}→地下鉄：01020_chikatetsu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{通勤|つうきん}している→通勤：03512_tsuukin⟧。
⟦{鉄道|てつどう}→鉄道：03550_tetsudou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{旅行|りょこう}する→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|す}きだ→好き：02355_suki⟧。

notes:
{鉄|てつ} refers to iron as a material, and by extension, steel and iron products.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {鉄道|てつどう}: railroad, railway
- {地下鉄|ちかてつ}: subway
- {鉄板|てっぱん}: iron plate, griddle; also slang for "guaranteed"
- {鉄砲|てっぽう}: gun, firearm
- {鉄橋|てっきょう}: iron bridge

EXPRESSIONS:
- {鉄|てつ}は{熱|あつ}いうちに{打|う}て: Strike while the iron is hot

SIMILAR MATERIALS:
- {銅|どう}: copper
- {銀|ぎん}: silver
- {金|きん}: gold
- {鋼|はがね}: steel (refined iron)

SLANG:
{鉄板|てっぱん} also means "guaranteed" or "sure thing" in modern slang.
